answer: A farm that wants 62 keys as a result pays 62 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the jetty seed, the vertex timing is verifiable from the pulse record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 317 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is inexpensive once and expensive in bulk. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
